interp.name: Interpolation error vs direct SPICE
interp.detail: 300 random off-grid times 2025-2032; max angle between the hourly-linear Sun/Earth direction and a direct SPICE spkpos call (MOON_ME, LT+S), either body.

sanity.name: South pole Sun elevation range, smooth sphere, 2025-2032
sanity.detail: max |Sun centre elevation| over hourly samples; min -1.587, max 1.587 deg. The lunar spin axis is tilted about 1.54 deg to the ecliptic.

illumination.name: Average sunlit %, Shackleton rim, 2025-2032 (any, 2 m) vs Glaeser et al. 2018
illumination.detail: Glaeser et al. 2018, Planet. Space Sci. 162, 170-178. Ours: any part of the Sun disc above the site horizon (2 m mast, 0.1 deg horizon), 6 h sampling 2025-01-01 to 2032-12-31. Differences: averaging period (paper: full 18.6 yr cycle), observer height, DEM resolution, and the exact rim point.

illumination.name: Average sunlit %, connecting ridge, 2025-2032 (any, 2 m)
illumination.detail: Informational: Glaeser et al. 2018 give a Shackleton rim figure only (compared above); the connecting ridge is checked against the PGDA raster below.

illumination.name: Average sunlit %, Shackleton rim, ours (2025-2032) vs PGDA/LOLA (Quickmap layer)
illumination.detail: Reference: NASA/GSFC PGDA (Mazarico et al.) AVGVISIB_75S_120M_201608, the same LOLA visibility data shown in LROC Quickmap; 120 m pixels, long-term average (LOLA 2009-2013 DEM). Ours: 6 h sampling 2025-2032, 2 m mast, 0.1 deg horizon; 'any' = any part of the Sun disc. Differences come from the averaging period, observer height, pixel size vs point, and horizon resolution.

eclipses.name: Lunar eclipse 2025-03-14: Sun fully covered at the site (0, 0) vs NASA U2/U3
eclipses.detail: Ours: first/last minute the Earth disc fully covers the Sun disc (spherical Earth, R 6371 km, no atmosphere enlargement) seen from the near-side point (0, 0). NASA: greatest eclipse 06:59:56 TD minus delta-T 75 s, and total duration 65.4 min split symmetrically (NASA lunar eclipse catalogue, Espenak/Meeus).

eclipses.name: Lunar eclipse 2025-03-14: totality (whole Moon disc in umbra, U2 to U3) vs NASA
eclipses.detail: Same Earth model (sphere R 6371 km, no atmosphere enlargement), but totality is defined as NASA defines U2/U3: every point on the lunar limb (as seen from the Sun) has the Sun fully covered by Earth.
